title: Character file
description: The standard interchange file for one character, monster or NPC. Holds only base state: input field values, owned content and per-copy state, choices made, and which temporary effects are on. Derived values are never saved. Every content and field reference is fully qualified (`pack:id`).

specVersion.description: The OCF spec version this file was written against.

id.description: An ID for this character. A UUID is fine for an ID unique within the app or campaign; a URL (IRI) makes it global, so the character keeps one identity across apps.

packs.description: The exact pack versions this character uses, in load order (later packs win).

creating.description: The character is being created. Default false, so a file without it is a finished character. An app sets it on a new character; the change `finishCreation` clears it once the character has no rules issues and no pending choices. Formulas read it as `character.creating`, so a constraint that holds only at creation guards on it.

values.description: Values of input fields, by qualified field ID. Missing fields take their default.

features.description: Owned content that is not carried: classes (with their level), feats, traits.

inventory.description: Carried content. The character's copy of an item is a base plus templates.

applied.description: Temporary effects from content the character doesn't own (Bless cast by an ally, a condition). The app turns them on and off; the engine never tracks time.

followUps.description: Ephemeral follow-ups: each `on` or `becomes` follow-up a batch triggered, stored by that applyChanges until it is acted on (`clearFollowUp`, which startAction proposes) or dismissed (`dismissFollowUp`). The engine writes them; apps change them only with those two changes. computeSheet lists each in `offers`. Derived (`while`) offers are never stored.

choices.description: Picks for character-level choices declared in the rules.

links.description: Which character fills each link slot, by qualified slot ID: the other character's `id`. How an app finds that character is the app's business.

homebrew.description: The character's own content and rules additions, loaded on top of the pinned packs as the pack `homebrew`, so the rest of the file refers to them as `homebrew:<id>`.

extensions.description: App-specific extras under each app's own namespace (reverse DNS or npm package name). Other apps carry them along untouched.

templates.description: Templates applied to this copy, in order.

choices.description: Picks for the choices declared by this item and its templates.

grants.description: Saved state of content this copy's item and templates grant (holder grants), by the granted content's qualified ID.

state.description: Per-copy state values by state key (charges, shots, level).

choiceTree.description: Picks keyed by choice ID. The tree's own item (the entry's item, or the picked option) uses bare choice IDs; choices declared by other content in the same tree (templates, granted content) are keyed `<qualified owner id>/<choice id>`. Each pick may carry the picks for the choices its option contains.

option.description: A qualified content ID, an inline option ID, or a value.

state.description: Values for state keys the picked content declares (its content type's or its own), as a copy's state. The picked content sees them as `self.<key>`; a key at its default is left out.

grants.description: Saved state of content the picked option grants (holder grants), by the granted content's qualified ID.

grantStore.description: Granted content's saved state, kept on the node whose choice tree holds its picks: a copy, or a pick. Each key is a granted item's qualified ID; `state` holds values for state keys it declares (its content type's or its own), as a pick's does. The granted content sees them as `self.<key>`, over the grant's `state` and the declared defaults; a key at that default is left out. The same item granted twice to one node shares it. Kept while the grant is off.

id.description: Unique among the character's stored follow-ups: `<the follow-up's own ID>-<n>`, the smallest n from 1 not in use.

followUp.description: The follow-up's ID: `<pack>:<id>` for the rules', `<content or type qualified ID>#<id>` for content's.

source.description: For a follow-up on content: the content and copy it comes from, as computeSheet's sources name them.

to.description: For a follow-up to a linked character: `{ link }` with the qualified slot ID. It is stored here, on the character whose change triggered it, since one applyChanges writes one file; the app shows it to whoever runs the linked character. Absent for the character's own.

character.description: For a follow-up to a link: the ID of the character filling the slot when it was triggered.

params.description: The parameters the follow-up fixes, evaluated when it was triggered.

cause.description: What triggered an `on` moment: the adjustment entry as the follow-up's formulas saw it as `change` (with `once`, the matching entries summed), and its field.
